issues.issue: The grant is 'for the sole purpose of' a long enumerated list of activities ending in general words about 'other structures, improvements, equipment and facilities', leaving the outer reach of the granted uses open to an ejusdem generis argument.
The stated 6,051.92 gross acres must be squared with the tract-by-tract acreages in Exhibit 'A', several of which are described only by approximations ('more or less', 'The North part of N/2 SE/4').
The habendum turns on production 'in commercial quantities', a term the Lease never defines, and on 'drilling or reworking operations ... as provided herein'.

The clause continues the whole Lease so long as production or operations occur anywhere on Said Land, while Paragraph 4(d) and 4(h) provide that after the Primary Term the Lease survives only drilling unit by drilling unit.

The royalty is set at 25% of 'the value of the gross production' but the same sentence equates that value to 'the proceeds received by Lessee', two measures that can diverge and that the clause does not reconcile.
The proceeds-based measure here sits against Paragraph 3(f)'s 'free of all costs' guarantee and Paragraph 3(d)'s 'market value at the plant' measure for liquids.

The deduction sentence is mangled — 'Any deduction for the expenses of ... shall be added to the price received by Lessee' — and the parenthetical exception ('Said transportation charges will be limited to direct for amounts of Lessor's gas transported') is ungrammatical and unclosed, leaving it genuinely unclear which post-production costs may be borne by Lessor.

The proviso guaranteeing proceeds 'equal to or greater than the proceeds received from sales in the field or prevailing area' and 'not less than received by Lessee or any of its affiliates' must be reconciled with Paragraph 3(f)'s absolute cost-free royalty and with Paragraph 3(d)'s market-value-at-the-plant measure.
'Sufficiently impregnated' and 'paying quantities ... as a practical lease operation' set no measurable threshold for when Lessee must install separation devices.

It applies the Paragraph 3(a) oil royalty to separated liquids while Paragraph 3(d) applies a market-value-at-the-plant royalty to liquids recovered by plant processing, so the boundary between lease-operation and plant recovery decides the measure.

'Market value at the plant' is undefined and the parenthetical listing indirect and direct costs ('amortization and depreciation on pipeline and plant investment and indirect overhead') may be read as exhaustive or merely illustrative.
The floor guarantee that 3(d) royalties 'shall never be less than' 3(b) royalties requires a shadow computation under Paragraph 3(b), whose own deduction language is defective.

'Free use ... for operations hereunder' does not say whether it covers fuel used off the leased premises or in compression, processing and transportation, and 'Royalties shall be computed after deducting any production so used' turns on that boundary.

Permitting royalty to be computed after deducting production used in operations is in tension with Paragraph 3(f)'s promise that royalties are delivered free of any production, compression, processing or transportation costs.
The list of excluded costs closes with the general phrase 'or like costs', leaving it uncertain which unenumerated post-production charges fall inside the cost-free promise.

The carve-out 'except as provided for in 3 (b) above' points to Paragraph 3(b), which itself says Lessor's royalty 'shall not be charged directly or indirectly with any such expenses' while carving out regulated transportation, so the two clauses must be reconciled to know what may be deducted.

The clause caps shut-in maintenance at 'two consecutive years from the date the well is shut-in' and then, after providing an increased $750 payment 'following the expiration of the two (2) year shut-in period', caps it again at 'three (3) consecutive years', an internal inconsistency about how long shut-in payments hold the Lease.

The opening condition is limited to wells shut in 'at any time during the Primary Term' and is expressly 'subject to the provisions of Paragraph 4(d)', yet later sentences govern wells shut in 'at or subsequent to the expiration of the Primary Term', requiring reconciliation with Paragraph 4(d)'s post-term retention rule.

'Interest at ten percent (10%) per annum for each day overdue to a maximum of one hundred, twenty (120) days' is unclear whether 120 days caps the accrual period or something else, and the first-payment trigger ends with 'whichever is the earliest' after only two alternatives.

The option may be exercised 'at any time, and from time to time' on 60 days' notice, yet any election 'shall be effective for a period of not less than twelve (12) months', leaving the interplay of the two limits uncertain.

Delivery of royalty gas 'at the wellhead after separation and dehydration' with all other costs borne by Lessor sits against Paragraph 3(f)'s promise that royalties are delivered free of separating, dehydration and transportation costs.

The closing sentence continues the Lease 'in the manner and for the time specified in Paragraph 4' — a circular self-reference to the whole of the paragraph it sits in, rather than to any identified sub-part.
It permits recommencement 'within the sixty (60) day period ... provided in Paragraph 4(b)', while Paragraph 4(b) also imposes a 30-day no-cessation requirement and Paragraph 4(c) a 60-day one.

This clause requires drilling operations to proceed 'with no cessation of more than thirty (30) consecutive days', while Paragraph 4(c) states that 'for all purposes of this Lease' operations are diligent if prosecuted without cessation of more than sixty (60) consecutive days.
The definition folds in 'a bona fide good faith effort' and 'a prudent manner with reasonable diligence', standards that are judgment-laden rather than measurable.

This sentence fixes 60 consecutive days as the diligence measure 'for all purposes of this Lease', which cannot be squared with Paragraph 4(b)'s requirement of no cessation of more than 30 consecutive days.

Notice is to be furnished 'with reasonable dispatch' and accompanied by 'any appropriate form required by the Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission', neither of which fixes a deadline or an identified form.

'Upon expiration of the Primary Term and completion of continuous drilling operations' is ambiguous as between the finishing of a continuous drilling programme and the cessation of one, and the retention test differs for oil ('producing') and gas ('capable of producing').

Paragraph 3(g) makes shut-in royalty 'subject to the provisions of Paragraph 4(d)', while 4(d) preserves the Lease only where 'shut-in royalties hav[e] been properly paid', so the two must be read together to know when a shut-in well saves the Lease.

It keys continuous operations to 'completion of operations under Paragraph 4(c)(ii) or 4(c)(iii)', but those sub-paragraphs merely define completion dates and prescribe no operations, so the cross-reference does not fit what it points to.

The Lease is said to 'terminate as to all depths which are one hundred (100) feet below the base of the deepest formation', which literally terminates only at that single depth rather than below it — a drafting slip that changes the depth actually released.
